title: Metabolite traffic: tracking chorismate and isochorismate reveals dynamics of aromatic metabolism
content: Plants synthesize a diverse array of metabolites that shape growth, defense, structural development, communication, and adaptation. This chemical diversity includes numerous aromatic specialized metabolites, most of which are produced via the shikimate pathway that takes place in plastids and leads to the production of chorismate (Fig. 1). Chorismate represents the last common precursor of aromatic amino acids (Phe, Tyr, Trp) and numerous other downstream metabolites including phenylpropanoids, lignin, and salicylic acid (El-Azaz and Maeda 2025; Boerjan et al. 2003). Although the shikimate pathway takes place in plastids, the downstream metabolism of its products extends across multiple cellular compartments.
